1.explanation:
• ReplaceConnectionBehavior.js  
  This is the behavior that listens for connection.reconnect events (i.e. dragging an association end to a new shape). It adjusts the DI waypoints but never considers updating the DI <bpmndi:BPMNEdge> parent container.  

• UpdateFlowNodeRefsHandler.js  
  This handler is invoked by the reconnect command to update the businessObject.sourceRef and targetRef of the association. It correctly rebinds the references, but it does not move the association out of the old element’s flowElements or adjust the DI parent.  

• UpdateSemanticParentHandler.js  
  This generic handler updates parent relationships for shapes when they are moved, but it isn’t wired up for reconnect operations on connections. It therefore never fires to reparent associations into their new BPMN container.  

• BpmnUpdater.js  
  This module applies semantic changes after modeling operations (e.g. adding/removing flow elements). It knows how to reparent sequence flows in the process.flowElements array, but lacks logic for associations. As a result, after reconnect the association remains listed in the old subprocess’s flowElements.

Together, these four files control reconnect behavior (ReplaceConnectionBehavior), the command that updates the connection’s source/target (UpdateFlowNodeRefsHandler), the DI/semantic reparenting logic (UpdateSemanticParentHandler), and the BPMN‐level update routines (BpmnUpdater). They all need to be extended to move an association into its new container when its endpoint is reconnected.
1.bug_scenario:
In the GIF the user drags one end of an association (the dotted line) out of a subprocess into its parent container. On the diagram the association’s end‐point visually moves, but under the covers the BPMN DI and the semantic parent of that association remain the old subprocess. Later, when the subprocess is deleted, its entire DI subtree (including the “moved” association) is removed as well.

In short: reconnecting an association endpoint does not update the association’s DI parent (and its BPMN parent in the semantic model), so it stays attached to the old subprocess and is inadvertently deleted when the subprocess goes away.

2.explanation:
All of these files are in the chain that moves and reconnects elements in the model and then re-wires their semantic parent.  

• UpdateSemanticParentHandler.js is the command handler responsible for actually updating the BPMN businessObject.$parent when an element is moved.  Associations are connections, but this handler only fires for shapes by default and never picks up the association on reconnect.  
• ReplaceConnectionBehavior.js is the behavior that kicks in when you reconnect one end of a connection. It ends up rerouting the dashed line visually, but it doesn’t call into the update-semantic-parent logic to move the association into the new container.  
• BpmnUpdater.js is the central synchronizer between the diagram’s moves and the underlying DI/semantic model. It needs to be augmented to detect when an association’s endpoints have moved out of their old parent and delegate to UpdateSemanticParentHandler to reparent the association’s businessObject under the new container.
2.bug_scenario:
When you drag both ends of an association (dashed line) out of a subprocess, the visual connection moves into the new container, but the underlying BPMN model still considers the association to be a child of the old subprocess. As a result, if you then delete the subprocess, the association goes away too even though visually it now lives in another plane.

In the GIF you can see that the small rectangle (source) and the association’s target bracket are both dropped outside of the subprocess, but the association stays behind when the subprocess is deleted.
